xAI has released Grok Build v1.0, marking a significant milestone in its effort to compete with Anthropic's Claude Code and OpenAI's Codex CLI in the terminal-based coding agent space. The stable release brings a complete UI overhaul, enhanced permission controls, and features designed to attract both developers and non-technical users.

The v1.0 update introduces richer permission prompts that display full scripts before execution, giving users complete visibility into what the agent will do before approval. Keyboard-handling fixes and improved SSH and tmux theme detection address long-standing pain points reported by early adopters. Perhaps most notably, Elon Musk personally announced the milestone and revealed plans to make Grok Build accessible to non-technical users—a significant pivot from its developer-focused origins.

## The Coding Agent Wars Intensify

Grok Build enters a rapidly expanding market. Anthropic's Claude Code has gained substantial traction among developers for its ability to handle complex multi-step tasks with minimal supervision. OpenAI's Codex CLI offers similar capabilities integrated with GitHub workflows. Now xAI is positioning Grok Build as a more transparent alternative with its distinctive personality and approach to agentic coding.

The terminal-based coding agent segment has become a key battleground because it represents the most immediate productivity gain for developers. Unlike chat-based assistants, these agents can execute commands, modify files, and run tests autonomously—making them both powerful and potentially risky.

## What's New in v1.0

The stable release includes several improvements that address feedback from the beta period. The UI overhaul brings a more intuitive interface for reviewing agent actions before they execute. Permission prompts now show complete scripts rather than summaries, allowing users to make fully informed decisions about agent activities.

xAI also improved compatibility with development environments, particularly around SSH connections and tmux sessions. These fixes were among the most requested by the developer community during the preview phase.

The roadmap toward non-technical accessibility suggests xAI sees broader market potential beyond individual developers. Potential use cases could include automated DevOps tasks, system administration, and workflow automation for teams without dedicated engineering resources.

The release comes amid increased competition in the AI coding agent space, with all major labs investing heavily in terminal-based tools that can reason about codebases and execute complex tasks autonomously.
